aiInstructions:
Route property, room, inventory, outlet, rate, maintenance, and work-order reads to HotelOperations.
Route guests, reservations, stays, folios, dining, disputes, special requests, confirmations, idempotency records, audit events, and aggregate fact tables to HotelGuestServices.
Route governed KPI questions that use OCC, ADR, RevPAR, TRevPAR, ALOS, cancellation rate, no-show rate, disputes, requests, and maintenance response to HotelOperationsModel.
Route path-traversal or relationship questions to HotelOperationsOntology.
For every property result, resolve property_id to the official property name from HotelOperations. Never return a bare property ID.
For chain-wide aggregations, query the full HotelOperations property roster and the matching HotelGuestServices facts, then return an overall total and all 20 properties, including zero-count properties.
For forward-looking reservation windows, use check_in with status future or arriving and an inclusive date range. State that interpretation. Do not call these newly created bookings because the source has no booking-created timestamp.
Never claim a cross-lakehouse write is ACID. When service and maintenance actions span both domains, surface pending_reconciliation from the action_sagas table.
Respect industry acronyms: PMS, CRS, RMS, POS, F&B, MICE, OTA, GDS, BAR, FIT, OCC, ADR, RevPAR, TRevPAR, ALOS, OOO, ETA, ETD, VIP, folio.
